title: When a Model Judge Certifies a Dataset: Asymmetric Over-Calling, Worker Clustering, and Unresolved Margins in Egocentric-10K
description: Commercial dataset vendors increasingly certify corpus quality with single-pass vision-language model statistics. Build AI reports that its Egocentric-10K corpus shows >=1 hand in 96.42% of frames and active manipulation in 91.66%, leading Ego4D and EPIC-KITCHENS-100, from 10,000 frames labelled once by gemini-2.5-flash with no human gold, no confidence interval, and no cross-domain check. Against 153 single-rater gold frames scored under a written rubric, the vendor's stored labels over-call >=1 hand on 9 of 24 at-risk frames (37.5%, 95% Wilson [21.2, 57.3]) and under-call 0 of 129 ([0.0, 2.9], p = 1.3e-8), and over-call active manipulation on 10 of 33 (30.3%) against 4 of 120 (3.3%, p = 3.4e-5). An independent open judge (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-FP8) shows the same asymmetry (6/24 vs. 0/129; 10/33 vs. 2/120). Second, on two 10,000-frame raw-corpus draws, camera-wearer clustering yields design effects of 1.25 to 1.66, widening intervals by 12 to 29% over iid (post-hoc factory clustering reaches 2.18 to 5.65); because evaluation releases omit grouping IDs, direct cluster-robust inference cannot run on the published sample. Third, PPI++ gold-correction over the vendor's 9,800-frame stored arms moves the active-manipulation lead over EPIC-KITCHENS-100 from +6.62 to -1.32 pp (iid 95% CI [-10.78, +8.14]; post-hoc cluster sensitivity [-11.28, +8.64] to [-12.07, +9.43]), leaving the lead unresolved. Resolving it takes roughly 89 gold frames per arm under iid (55 more than exist) and 93 to 115 under clustering. Because all 153 labels are single-rater and the vendor's judge reverses on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 manipulation, an independent second rater is needed before generalising this asymmetry into an upper-bound claim. Not peer reviewed.
